exposure: Birth asphyxia (temporary occlusion of the umbilical cord)
outcome: Motor development (neonatal arousal, physical activity, gait test parameters)
Glial fibrillary acidic protein levels in CSF
Expression of genes related to oxidative stress, inflammation, and synaptic functions
Number of apoptotic cells among CTIP2-positive neurons and striatal medium spiny neurons
cohort: Newborn caesarean-delivered pigs were used as an animal model for birth asphyxia.
finding: Dietary plasma supplementation in asphyxiated pigs improved gait performance, attenuated neuronal apoptosis, and affected gene expression related to neuroinflammation, neurotransmission, and antioxidants in the motor cortex and caudate.
